tool_search.description: Find tools by keyword. Returns matching tool names with descriptions and argument schemas; the tools you find become callable on your next step. Use this before saying you cannot do something.

query.description: Keywords describing what you need, e.g. "read file" or "search web"

conversation_search.description: Search earlier conversations by meaning. Returns the most similar past messages that you are allowed to see, with who said them and when. Use it to recall facts, decisions or preferences from before.

query.description: What to look for, in natural language

now.description: The current date and time: UTC and, for an IANA time zone, the local time, weekday and UTC offset. Use it whenever the answer depends on today, now, a deadline or opening hours.

timezone.description: IANA time zone, e.g. "Africa/Cairo" or "America/New_York" (default UTC)

math_calc.description: Evaluate a math expression instead of computing in your head: + - * / % ** and parentheses, comparisons and cond ? a : b, and abs, ceil, floor, round, int, float, min, max, sum, mean, median (lists are [1, 2.5]). Example: round((19.99 * 3) * 0.85 * 100) / 100. Use it for totals, prices, discounts, splits and any arithmetic.

ask_user.description: Ask the person you are talking to 1-10 structured questions, batched into ONE call, when the answers change what you do next (never for what you can decide or look up yourself). They pause the conversation as a form the person fills; your next tool result carries their answers. Keep every question self-contained.

id.description: [a-z0-9_] up to 40 chars, unique in this call

type.description: single = one choice, multi = any of the choices, text = free text, confirm = yes/no

placeholder.description: text only: hint seen in the empty textarea

task.description: A complete, self-contained task. The specialist sees nothing else from this conversation.
